assignedLines.text: Shortly after eight the next morning, Sheila walked home to change for church. What she found sent her screaming from the cabin.
assignedLines.camera: close push-in, host centered; rising dread

assignedLines.text: Her mother lay dead on the living room floor. Beside her — her brother John, and his friend Dana. All three bound and broken.
assignedLines.camera: arc move left around host, ending front-center; raw grief, controlled

assignedLines.text: The walls were splattered with blood. But in the back bedroom, three little boys — Rick, Greg, and their friend Justin — slept on. Unharmed.
assignedLines.camera: slight high-angle tilt-down to eye level; disbelief, horror

assignedLines.text: They had heard nothing. Seen nothing. Three children, asleep feet from a massacre — and untouched.
assignedLines.camera: push from soft blur to sharp medium shot; stunned, hollow

assignedLines.text: One person was missing. Twelve-year-old Tina Sharp was nowhere in the cabin. Not alive. Not dead. Just — gone.
assignedLines.camera: lateral dolly right-to-left, close framing; chilling, low voice

assignedLines.text: The killers had brought their own tools — knives, a hammer — and stayed for hours. This was no burglary. This was personal.
assignedLines.camera: static close-up, then subtle forward-lean drift; hard anger beneath control
